newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ to close consulates in Melboure, Brisbane.
newsitem.headline: NZ to close consulates in Melboure, Brisbane.

text.p: New Zealand said on Monday it will close its consulates in the Australian cities of Melbourne and Brisbane later this year.
"New Zealand consular assistance in Australia will be streamlined to concentrate resources in Canberra and Sydney," Foreign Affairs Minister Don McKinnon said in a statement.
"The requirement for physical representation in Melbourne and Brisbane has decreased and we will be closing these consulates later in the year."
McKinnon said New Zealanders in Australia would continue to be served by the New Zealand High Commission in Canberra and the Consulate General in Sydney.
He said the decision to close the Melbourne and Brisbane offices had not been taken lightly. Dates and details of the closures were still being planned.
"Australia is still our most important partner and we will continue to maintain a strong diplomatic, commercial and consular presence there."
McKinnon said the ease of contact between the New Zealand government and Australian State governments had to some extent offset the need for permanent offices in Melbourne and Brisbane.
